title: Adic completion is Noetherian when the quotient is Noetherian and the ideal finitely generated
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq R$ an ideal such that (1) the quotient ring $R/I$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and (2) $I$ is finitely generated. Let $R^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR/I^n$ be the $I$-adic completion of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and $IR^\wedge$ the ideal of $R^\wedge$ generated by the image of $I$ under the canonical map $R\to R^\wedge$. Then $R^\wedge$ is a Noetherian ring and $R^\wedge$ is $IR^\wedge$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, line 23011); used in the proof of Lemma Tag 0328 (lemma-cohen-rings-exist, line 44878). Generalizes Lemma Tag 0316 (lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian, the case R Noetherian), which is the node lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian

proof.text: (Completeness; reduction.) Put $A=R^\wedge$ with canonical map $\iota:R\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and $J=IR^\wedge$. Choose generators $f_1,\ldots,f_t$ of $I$ (hypothesis (2)); then $J$ is generated by $g_i=\iota(f_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,t$ (each $\iota(x)$, $x=\sum r_if_i\in I$, equals $\sum\iota(r_i)g_i$). By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] ($I$ finitely generated) $A$ is $J$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], which is the second assertion, and $A/J\cong R/I$ as rings. Since $R/I$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and the isomorphism $R/I\to A/J$ is a surjective ring map, $A/J$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. It remains to show: a ring $A$ that is $J$-adically complete for an ideal $J=(g_1,\ldots,g_t)$ with $A/J$ Noetherian is Noetherian (steps 2-6).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, line 23011), proof, first paragraph (lines 23023-23029), citing Lemma Tag 05GG (lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, line 22645)

proof.text: (The associated graded ring is Noetherian.) Let $G=\operatorname{gr}_J(A)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}J^n/J^{n+1}$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], an $A/J$-algebra, and $\bar g_i=g_i\bmod J^2\in J/J^2$. By the universal property of the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] there is an $A/J$-algebra map $\varphi:(A/J)[T_1,\ldots,T_t]\to G$ with $T_i\mapsto\bar g_i$; for $a\in A$ and a monomial $T^E$, $|E|=n$, it sends $(a\bmod J)T^E$ to $ag^E\bmod J^{n+1}$, $g^E=g_1^{e_1}\cdots g_t^{e_t}$. $\varphi$ is surjective: $J^n$ is generated as an ideal by the products $g^E$ with $|E|=n$ (products of $n$ generators of $J$), so every element of $J^n$ is $\sum_{|E|=n}a_Eg^E$, $a_E\in A$, and its class in $J^n/J^{n+1}$ is $\varphi(\sum_E(a_E\bmod J)T^E)$; $G$ is the sum of these homogeneous pieces. Hence $G\cong(A/J)[T_1,\ldots,T_t]/\ker\varphi$ as $A/J$-algebras is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $A/J$ (step 1), so $G$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, line 23011), proof, second paragraph, lines 23031-23035

proof.text: (Homogeneous generators of the initial ideal.) Let $K\subseteq A$ be an ideal. For $n\ge0$ the map $K\cap J^n\to J^n/J^{n+1}$ has kernel $K\cap J^{n+1}$; let $G(K)_n\subseteq J^n/J^{n+1}$ be its image (so $G(K)_n\cong K\cap J^n/K\cap J^{n+1}$, Stacks' notation) and $G(K)=\bigoplus_nG(K)_n\subseteq G$. $G(K)$ is a homogeneous ideal of $G$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]: it is a graded subgroup, and for $b\in J^m$, $x\in K\cap J^n$ the product $(b\bmod J^{m+1})(x\bmod J^{n+1})=bx\bmod J^{n+m+1}$ with $bx\in K\cap J^{n+m}$; by biadditivity this gives closure under multiplication by all of $G$. As $G$ is Noetherian (step 2) [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $G(K)$ is generated by finitely many elements; replacing each by its homogeneous components (which lie in $G(K)$, as $G(K)$ is homogeneous) we get homogeneous generators $\bar h_1,\ldots,\bar h_m$ of $G(K)$, $\bar h_j\in G(K)_{d_j}$, and we choose $h_j\in K\cap J^{d_j}$ with $h_j\bmod J^{d_j+1}=\bar h_j$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, line 23011), proof, second paragraph, lines 23036-23045 (the ideal $\bigoplus J\cap I^n/J\cap I^{n+1}$ and its homogeneous generators $\bar g_j$ of degree $d_j$ with lifts $g_j\in J\cap I^{d_j}$; Stacks' $J$ is our $K$, Stacks' $g_j$ our $h_j$)

proof.text: (One approximation step.) Let $n\ge0$ and $x\in K\cap J^n$. Then there are $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in A$ with $a_j\in J^{\max(0,n-d_j)}$, $a_j=0$ if $d_j>n$, and $x-\sum_ja_jh_j\in K\cap J^{n+1}$. Indeed $\bar x=x\bmod J^{n+1}\in G(K)_n$, so $\bar x=\sum_j\beta_j\bar h_j$ with $\beta_j\in G$ (step 3); comparing the components of degree $n$ we may replace $\beta_j$ by its component of degree $n-d_j$ when $d_j\le n$ and by $0$ when $d_j>n$; write that component as $a_j\bmod J^{n-d_j+1}$ with $a_j\in J^{n-d_j}$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Then $\bar x=\sum_j(a_jh_j\bmod J^{n+1})$, i.e. $x-\sum_ja_jh_j\in J^{n+1}$, and this element lies in $K$ because $x,h_j\in K$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, line 23011), proof, third paragraph, lines 23047-23051

proof.text: (Iteration.) Let $x\in K$. Put $x_0=x\in K\cap J^0$ and, given $x_n\in K\cap J^n$, choose by step 4 elements $a_{j,n}\in J^{\max(0,n-d_j)}$ ($a_{j,n}=0$ if $d_j>n$) with $x_{n+1}=x_n-\sum_ja_{j,n}h_j\in K\cap J^{n+1}$. By induction on $N$, $x=\sum_{n=0}^N\sum_{j=1}^ma_{j,n}h_j+x_{N+1}$ with $x_{N+1}\in J^{N+1}$, for every $N\ge0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 05GH (lemma-completion-Noetherian, line 23011), proof, third paragraph, lines 23051-23059

proof.text: (Convergence; conclusion.) Fix $j$ and put $s_{j,N}=\sum_{n=0}^Na_{j,n}$. For $N'\ge N\ge d_j$ we have $s_{j,N'}-s_{j,N}=\sum_{n=N+1}^{N'}a_{j,n}\in J^{N+1-d_j}$. Hence for each $k\ge1$ the class $s_{j,N}\bmod J^k$ is the same for all $N\ge k+d_j$; call it $y_{j,k}$. The family $(y_{j,k})_k$ is compatible, i.e. an element of $\varprojlim_kA/J^k$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; since $A$ is $J$-adically complete (step 1) [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], the canonical map $A\to\varprojlim_kA/J^k$ is bijective and there is $A_j\in A$ with $A_j-s_{j,N}\in J^k$ whenever $N\ge k+d_j$. Now let $k\ge1$ and $N=k+\max_jd_j$; by step 5, $x-\sum_jA_jh_j=x_{N+1}+\sum_j(s_{j,N}-A_j)h_j\in J^{N+1}+J^k=J^k$. So $x-\sum_jA_jh_j\in\bigcap_kJ^k$, which is $0$ because $A\to\varprojlim_kA/J^k$ is injective. Thus $x=\sum_jA_jh_j$, and since $h_j\in K$, $K=(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$ is finitely generated. As $K$ was arbitrary, $A=R^\wedge$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

split_report.summary: Split along the proof of Stacks 05GH (algebra.tex lines 23022-23063), tags 05GH, 05GG, 00FN verified in tags/tags. Step 1: completeness of R^ w.r.t. IR^ and R^/IR^ = R/I from the existing leaf lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal (05GG), Noetherianity of R^/IR^ via lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian, reduction to a J-adically complete A with J=(g_1..g_t), A/J Noetherian. Step 2: gr_J(A) is a quotient of (A/J)[T_1..T_t] (def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring), hence Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian. Steps 3-6: the initial ideal G(K) of an ideal K has homogeneous generators lifting to h_j in K, the approximation x - sum a_j h_j in K cap J^{n+1}, the iteration, and the convergence of A_j = sum_n a_{j,n} by completeness, with x - sum A_j h_j in the intersection of the J^k, which is 0; written out where Stacks says 'as R is complete'. New node: def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring (unsplit, not in Mathlib). Not a Mathlib leaf (LeanSearch, LeanFinder, Loogle, grep). Statement unchanged; stmt_deps unchanged.
